conflict.summary: Eleven wired integrations, nine files. The type agrees (boolean) and every wired file answers from activity, never from a logging setting, so the configured-versus-activity split recorded on isIAMLoggingEnabled applies here too, with no configured side yet. Inside the activity side the files still disagree on recency (none, 3 days, 90 days) and on whether an empty read is false or not measured, so the same quiet tenant reads false at Okta, Azure AD, Britive, Saviynt and Zscaler and Not evaluated at Duo and JumpCloud. Separately: at Okta the isAuditLoggingEnabled file and is_mfa_logging_enabled.py run the same affirmative_signal over the same getAuditLogging read, so isAuditLoggingEnabled, isMFALoggingEnabled and isIAMLoggingEnabled are one value under three names there.

proposedResolution.summary: Rule this key together with isIAMLoggingEnabled, whose open proposal keeps the logging-key name for a configured state and moves record-presence answers to a presence key whose empty read is not_measured. No file here reads a configuration, so under that proposal every wired position would move and this name would be left with no implementation until one reads a setting. Settle recency (none, 3 days, 90 days) as part of the same ruling, and decide separately whether an accepted export job (Safe Security) is evidence for any logging key.

decision.question: Does isAuditLoggingEnabled mean 'audit logging is configured on' or 'audit records were returned', how recent must the newest record be, and is an empty read false or not measured? Is it one key with isIAMLoggingEnabled (and, at Okta, isMFALoggingEnabled), since Okta answers all three from one read?
